T0618.title: Marketing Loss
T0618.definition: Marketing loss is the direct monetary or resource loss caused when coupons, subsidies, rebates, red packets, points, or gifts are used outside their intended marketing rules.
T0618.description:
Marketing loss commonly appears in unlimited coupon claiming, discount stacking arbitrage, coupon usage restriction bypass, repeated first-order rewards, fake referral growth, and order-splitting arbitrage. The loss is not limited to cash subsidies; it can also include gifts, points, inventory, ad budgets, acquisition rewards, and merchant-funded discounts.

Unlike normal marketing cost, marketing loss emphasizes that marketing resources are exploited unexpectedly through rule flaws or gray-market behavior. Governance needs to combine campaign budgets, discount ratios, refund rollback, product flow, and account linkage in one monitoring loop, rather than looking only at individual orders.
T0618.usageExample: After a major campaign, the review found an abnormal increase in discount ratios and attributed it to marketing loss caused by a discount stacking flaw.
